articles.title: Palantir and Shopify Both Beat Earnings. Their Stocks are Falling Anyway.
articles.summary:
Apple, Palantir, Shopify, and several other major companies just reported earnings, and Wall Street is sending a clear message: Beating expectations isn't enough when profit margins are under pressure.

In this video, Eric Bleeker, CFA, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., breaks down the biggest earnings movers and what their results reveal about the stock market.

Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) beat revenue and earnings expectations as iPhone sales surged 17.5%, but disappointing gross margins raised concerns. Palantir (Nasdaq: PLTR) delivered explosive 96% revenue growth, yet investors are questioning slower growth in U.S. commercial contract value.

Shopify (NYSE: SHOP) plunged 16% after missing revenue expectations and disappointing on free cash flow, despite beating earnings estimates.

Elsewhere, Revvity (NYSE: RVTY) rallied 9% after raising guidance, while Fiserv (Nasdaq: FISV) jumped 10% on stronger earnings and expanded cost-cutting plans.

Meanwhile, Zebra Technologies (Nasdaq: ZBRA) tumbled 16% despite beating estimates and raising its outlook, and Dynatrace (NYSE: DT) cut earnings guidance due to margin pressures.

The big takeaway? Investors are increasingly focused on profitability, margins, and forward guidance rather than headline earnings beats alone.

articles.title: Money 20/20 USA: Thunes Deputy CEO Chloe Mayenobe on everyday use of stablecoins
articles.summary: Chloe Mayenobe, Deputy CEO of Thunes, sits down with JD Durkin at Money 20/20 USA in Las Vegas to explain how Thunes connects the digital asset world with traditional banking rails, moving money instantly across 140 countries and 90 currencies under more than 50 licenses. Mayenobe walks through a busy stretch of partnerships: a new alliance with Coinbase, JPMorgan Payments choosing Thunes to help Chase account holders reach bank accounts and mobile wallets worldwide, and a deal with Fiserv that lets merchants pay suppliers, workers and partners around the globe. She also shares why, despite the US being the world’s top sender of cross-border payments, those payments are still seen as slow and opaque, and why that’s a big opportunity for Thunes.
